newsitem.title: POLAND: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon reiterates WBK buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon reiterates WBK buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers in London said it reiterated its buy rating for Poland's Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK), in part due to integration with 60.2-percent owner AIB. "Following the recent easing of the WBK share price, we view the stock as attractive and reiterate our buy code with a target price of 25 zlotys," the report dated August 5 said.
WBK shares on Tuesday closed at 18.3 zlotys.
The report said WBK, trading at 18.2 zlotys at the time of the report, was trading at 7.3 times Salomon's 1997 net profit forecast and 1.9 times projected book value for end-1997.

"With ROE (return on equity) projected at around 32 percent versus forecast inflation of 15 percent, a cost-to-income ratio of 46 percent and net non-performing loans of just 5.6 percent at end-1996, WBK's financial profile and long-term earnings outlook appears to be dimly reflected in current valuations," the report said.

It said WBK shares looked attractive especially compared to West European bank valuations, which had seen broad earnings multiple expansion in 1997, and to a lesser degree to European and international developing market banking valuations.

Salomon saw WBK's lending growth this year at 40 percent, which it said would prove more sustainable than last year's 60 percent. It said WBK should lift net income to 174.9 million zlotys in 1998 from 171.3 million zlotys this year and last year's 168 million zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
